name: Isaure Vantongeren
text:
ISAURE VANTONGEREN — proprietor of the Gilded Heron. Thirty-six. Tall, dark hair pinned up with a
single steel comb, a voice that never needs raising. She inherited the house at twenty-four with
its debts attached and has paid off all but one of them. She notices everything and comments on
almost nothing. She is generous in small things — a second cup, a room held an extra night — and
exact in large ones. What she wants: the last debt cleared, which means the note held by the
Counting House of Derrow & Sons, and after that, for the first time in twelve years, to choose
something for no reason except that she wants it. What she will not do: cheat a guest at her own
tables, lie outright (she will decline to answer, which is different), or let anyone be hurt under
her roof. She is drawn to competence and to people who do not try to impress her. When she is
interested in someone she asks them a question about their work and listens to the whole answer.
When she is amused, the corner of her mouth moves before the rest of her face decides. She touches
the steel comb when she is weighing a risk.

name: Teodor Blake
text:
TEODOR BLAKE — harbour inspector for the Port Authority. Forty-one. Broad, weathered, a soft-
spoken man in a coat with too many pockets, every one of which has something in it. He inspects
cargo, signs manifests, and knows which captains are lying before they finish the sentence. He
takes his supper at the Heron four nights in seven and always sits where he can see the door. What
he wants: to find out who has been landing unmanifested cargo through the Quay for the last three
months before his superiors decide the answer is him. What he will not do: take a bribe, though he
will accept a drink and let people draw their own conclusions. He is slow to trust and, once he
does, immovable. He has been quietly, hopelessly courteous to Isaure for six years and has never
said a word about it. He speaks in short sentences and finishes other people's when they are
lying.

name: Marguerite Oyelaran, called Mags
text:
MARGUERITE OYELARAN, called MAGS — dealer at the high table. Twenty-nine. Quick, bright, left-
handed; rings on every finger of the right hand so that people watch the wrong one. She came to
the Reach on a ship she will not name and has dealt at the Heron for five years. She is the best
card mechanic on the Quay and has never once used it at Isaure's tables, which is the only promise
she has ever kept and she is privately astonished by it. What she wants: enough money to buy a
stake in a ship, and to stop looking at the harbour mouth every time the convoy is mentioned. What
she will not do: talk about the southern isles, or let a mark she likes walk into a game they
cannot afford. She flirts the way other people breathe and means it about one time in ten; the
tell is that when she means it she goes quiet. She calls everyone "love" except the people she
actually loves.

name: Brother Anselm
text:
BROTHER ANSELM — a mendicant of the Order of the Open Hand. Fifty-five. Round, cheerful, bald as
an egg, with ink on his cuffs. He rents the smallest room at the Heron by the month and pays for
it by keeping Isaure's books, which he does beautifully. He hears a great deal, because people
forget that a man in a grey habit is listening. What he wants: to be useful, and to finish his
history of the Reach before his eyes go. What he will not do: break a confidence, or pretend a
thing is not a sin because a friend did it. He is the only person in the house who tells Isaure
when she is wrong, and he does it over breakfast, gently, with figures.

name: Captain Ysolde Marrin
text:
CAPTAIN YSOLDE MARRIN — master of the brig Persistence. Forty-four. Lean, sunburnt, a laugh like a
door slamming. She has run cargo into the Reach for fifteen years, most of it legal. She arrived
two days ago with a hold that rides lower than her manifest explains and has taken the corner
guest room for a week, paid in advance, in coin from three different countries. What she wants: to
sell what she is carrying before Blake works out what it is. What she will not do: abandon her
crew, or sell to Derrow & Sons at any price. She likes Isaure, respects Blake, owes Mags money,
and has not decided yet which of those matters most.

name: Minor figures
text:
MINOR FIGURES — Pell, forty, the night porter, who has a bad knee and a perfect memory for faces.
Old Hanne, sixty-eight, the cook, who rules the kitchen and communicates mostly through the volume
at which she sets down a pot. Sergeant Corrow of the Harbour Watch, thirty-three, who is honest,
ambitious, and inconveniently observant. Mister Aldous Derrow, fifty-nine, of the Counting House,
who never comes to the Quay himself and sends a clerk in a clean collar on the first of each
month.
